title: Onboarding bakeoff — signal comparison and decision brief
content:
Summary:

This note summarizes the Q1 2026 onboarding bakeoff comparing four candidate model variants for the customer-facing summarization + support triage pipeline. The goal was to evaluate trade-offs across signal (helpfulness, factuality), regressions vs the current production baseline (prod-7b-v1), and operational metrics (latency, token cost). This is a working decision brief intended for product + infra sign-off.

Short recommendation (tentative):
- Promote rdw-7b-inst-v2-q to staged Dedicated rollout (50% traffic) for two weeks, with aggressive monitoring on hallucination slices and latency p95. rdw-7b-inst-v2-q shows the best balance of helpfulness gains with an acceptable cost increase.

Experiment setup: 
- Dataset: 3k evaluation items sampled from production prompts (support tickets, chat transcripts, and FAQ rewrite requests) stratified into: 40% short queries, 40% multi-turn support, 20% long-context summarization.
- Prompt sets: three curated templates (See below).
- Baseline: prod-7b-v1 (the current serving model).
- Candidates: rdw-7b-inst-v1, rdw-7b-inst-v2-q (quantized + instruction-tuned), rdw-13b-instruct-lite, open-13b-quant (community model).
- Metrics: Helpfulness (human-rated 1-5 mapped to 0-100), Hallucination rate (human labels %), Exact-match time-sensitive facts (F1-ish), p95 latency (ms, 8k context), cost per 1k tokens (USD estimate).
- Stats: paired bootstrap for confidence intervals; significance threshold p < 0.05 versus baseline.

Prompt sets used (short descriptions):
- Prompt A (triage-short): single-turn support question -> label intent + short summary (used for short queries).
- Prompt B (support-thread): multi-turn thread summarization + suggested next action (used for support transcripts).
- Prompt C (long-summarize): condense long context ( > 2000 tokens) into a 3-bullet summary with source pointers.

Leaderboards (aggregated results):

Model                         | Helpfulness | Hallucination % | Fact-F1 | p95 Latency ms | Cost / 1k toks
------------------------------|-------------|-----------------|---------|----------------|---------------
prod-7b-v1 (baseline)         | 68.4        | 7.8             | 72.1    | 280            | $0.45
rdw-7b-inst-v1               | 71.9        | 6.9             | 74.3    | 300            | $0.50
rdw-7b-inst-v2-q             | 77.3        | 8.5             | 76.0    | 320            | $0.40
rdw-13b-instruct-lite        | 79.1        | 11.2            | 80.5    | 460            | $0.95
open-13b-quant               | 66.7        | 13.5            | 68.2    | 420            | $0.35

Interpretation notes on leaderboard: 
- rdw-7b-inst-v2-q: largest helpfulness uplift (+8.9 absolute vs baseline) with slightly higher measured hallucination rate; cost per 1k tokens is lower due to quantization improvements in runtime. 
- rdw-13b-instruct-lite: highest factuality (Fact-F1) but p95 latency and cost are materially higher; may only be suitable for high-value support lanes.
- open-13b-quant: cheaper but shows regressions in helpfulness and factuality, and high hallucination rate — not recommended for production customer-facing paths.

Win/Loss vs baseline (pairwise on 3k samples):
- rdw-7b-inst-v2-q: Wins 44% | Losses 22% | Ties 34% (win delta concentrated on multi-turn support prompts)
- rdw-7b-inst-v1: Wins 28% | Losses 20% | Ties 52%
- rdw-13b-instruct-lite: Wins 51% | Losses 30% | Ties 19%
- open-13b-quant: Wins 18% | Losses 50% | Ties 32%

Significance / regression detection: 
- rdw-7b-inst-v2-q vs baseline: helpfulness uplift is significant (p = 0.004). Hallucination increase is small but measurable; delta = +0.7% absolute on a base of 7.8% (p = 0.07) — not significant at 0.05 but flagged.
- rdw-13b-instruct-lite shows significant improvement in Fact-F1 (p < 0.01) but latency/cost trade-offs are large.
- open-13b-quant fails at helpfulness and factuality metrics with p < 0.01, so treated as a regression.

Slice analysis (important regressions identified):
- Time-sensitive facts (billing / dates): rdw-7b-inst-v2-q shows a slight uptick in hallucination on date normalization prompts (sampled error modes: invented deadlines). Action: add a post-filter for date normalization or a small retrieval signal.
- Multi-turn memory (>4 turns): rdw-7b-inst-v2-q consistently outperforms baseline on relevance and suggested actions.
- Long context (>3500 tokens): 13b gives better summarization fidelity, but latency exceeds SLO. Consider hybrid routing for long-context jobs.

Operational metrics and infra notes: 
- rdw-7b-inst-v2-q quantized path reduces cost by ~11% in throughput tests vs rdw-7b-inst-v1 but shows ~10% higher p95 latency due to kernel packing overhead at 8k context. We measured CPU/GPU utilization traces in staging (linked).
- Serving knobs to test during staged rollout: dynamic batching thresholds, KV cache warmup policy, and prefix caching lifetimes.

Decision rationale and proposed rollout plan: 
1) Staged rollout: promote rdw-7b-inst-v2-q to Dedicated staging at 50% traffic for a 14-day evaluation window. Configure canary rule: route only threads classified as low time-sensitivity to start.
2) Monitoring: add the following watches (we will enable alerts):
   - rolling 24h hallucination rate > baseline + 2% absolute -> auto rollback.
   - helpfulness mean drops below baseline -> incident.
   - p95 latency > baseline * 1.6 for > 30m -> scaling/rollback.
3) Safety mitigations: enable fallback model (prod-7b-v1) for routes that fail factuality heuristics or exceed token budget.
4) Long-term: run a follow-up bakeoff that includes hybrid routing with rdw-13b-instruct-lite for long context jobs and measure end-to-end latency/cost impact.

Action items / TODOs: 
- [ ] Product: confirm which customer segments can be routed to staged rollout (Benji).
- [ ] Infra: add post-filter hook for date normalization (Marco).
- [ ] SRE: setup the hallucination alert and rollback automation (Sofia).
- [ ] Eval: expand prompt set C by 2k more long-context items and re-run (Aisha).

Open questions / risks: 
- The measured hallucination uptick on rdw-7b-inst-v2-q may be dataset-specific (we used a higher proportion of ambiguous support prompts). Need a second independent sample before final decision.
- Quantized runtimes can hide edge-case failures; we should increase fuzz tests on tokenization and rounding.

Appendix (short):
- Representative failure examples: see linked gist (JIRA-ML-4821) — includes three cases where the model invented policy names and one case of date hallucination.
- Quick links: Confluence experiment page, evaluation harness notebook, MR for model artifact.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working doc. If you disagree with the 50% staging approach, propose specific thresholds for promotion. 

-- Aisha Khan (eng-applied-ml)
